title: eriogonum kearneyi subsp. monoense
intro: Eriogonum kearneyi subsp. monoense, commonly known as Mono Mormon tea, is a plant species that belongs to the buckwheat family (Polygonaceae) and is native to the southwestern United States. This plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include relief from colds, coughs, and respiratory issues due to its health benefits of acting as an expectorant and anti-inflammatory agent. The therapeutic actions of Eriogonum kearneyi subsp. monoense include stimulating coughs, reducing fever, and alleviating congestion, primarily attributed to its ability to induce sweating and promote the removal of mucus. The bioactive constituents responsible for these actions are primarily alkaloids and flavonoids, although further research is needed to fully identify and understand the plant's chemical composition.
